name: copy_sixteen_longs_then_call
description: If the destination pointer passed on the stack is non-null, copies sixteen 32-bit values from a fixed offset in a structure held in a register into that destination, then jumps through a function pointer held in another register.

name: entry_dispatch_workbench_or_cli
description: Program entry point that finds the running process and branches on whether it was started from the CLI. The CLI branch splits the command-line text into space-separated words and passes them to the main routine, while the Workbench branch runs setup and cleanup library calls.

name: release_message_and_return
description: Passes its argument to a library routine, then if a shared flag is set it disables multitasking and replies to a message, and finally returns the stored argument.

name: call_two_library_vectors
description: Calls two library functions one after the other through a library base register, using two fixed offsets below that base, and returns.

name: attempt_library_call_else_release
description: Returns the result of one library call when it is nonzero; otherwise it calls another library function, stores the value 100 as an argument, runs the same finishing sequence as the release routine, and returns that argument.

name: switch_cli_icon_files
description: Sets default timing values on one branch, then uses the dos rename call on the CLI.info and CLI.noinfo icon files in the system directory to switch between them, depending on a stored choice.

name: open_libraries_and_setup_screen
description: Opens the graphics and intuition libraries and builds the preferences screen state, copying settings into the display records and returning 1 on success. If an open fails, it loops indefinitely.

name: wait_and_drain_message_port
description: Waits on a message port's signal bit, reads the messages queued there and replies to each one. It returns a code derived from the first message received.

name: close_preferences_resources
description: Releases the preferences program's resources by closing the library handles held in globals and calling one further library function.

name: run_handler_for_type_codes
description: Returns the result of a sub-routine only when a type code read from the current item is 32, 33 or 64; for any other code it returns zero.

name: write_two_preference_entries
description: Calls the same setter routine twice, once with selector 0 and once with selector 1, passing an address computed from the current preferences record and the caller's value.

name: write_preference_table_entries
description: Writes a block of stored values into indexed settings: with a selector of zero it writes three entries from one table, otherwise it writes four entries from a second table.

name: set_colour_from_rgb_word
description: Splits a 12-bit colour word into red, green and blue nibbles and passes them with a colour index to the graphics library's colour-setting call. Any index above 4 is replaced by zero.

name: initialize_object_record_table
description: Builds a table of 93 fixed-size records, linking each to the next and classifying each by a type value to set its pointers. It then computes a few position and size fields from stored settings and returns zero.

name: dispatch_preference_action_code
description: Switches on an action code read from an item record and runs the matching case, which adjusts preference settings through library calls, updates display settings or resets window state, and returns a value telling the caller what to do next.

name: format_countdown_digits
description: Writes a fixed separator sequence into the text buffer, then writes two decimal values, computed from a stored base value and a count from a sub-routine, as digit characters.

name: convert_day_count_to_date
description: Converts a day count into a year, month and day by repeatedly subtracting month lengths of 30 and 31 days, then passes the year, month and day to the date text formatter.

name: format_three_two_digit_fields
description: Writes three values as two-digit decimal pairs into the text buffer, in the order second, third and first argument, with no separators.

name: draw_fixed_screen_text
description: Issues a fixed sequence of drawing calls on the given rastport, setting a few drawing parameters and drawing two text strings at set coordinates, then returns zero.

name: parse_typed_date_to_daycount
description: Parses a typed date and time from the global text buffer: two-digit year, month and day, then hours and minutes. It converts the date to a day count using a fixed offset and passes that count and the total minutes to a setter.

name: clamp_and_roll_date_fields
description: Corrects the typed day, month and year digits in the global text buffer, rolling a day past the end of its month into the next month with a leap-year check for February, then writes the corrected values back as two-digit fields.

name: advance_year_month_on_overflow
description: Carries a month value above twelve into the next year, wraps the two-digit year after 99 back to zero, and passes the result to the date formatter.

name: borrow_date_fields_to_valid
description: Corrects the typed date for a backward step: a day below one borrows from the previous month, and February is limited to 28 or 29 days by a leap-year check before the fields are formatted.

name: wrap_month_and_year_backward
description: Wraps a month below one to December of the previous year, wraps a year below zero to 99, and passes the result to the date formatter.

name: refresh_setting_indicators
description: When its flag argument is nonzero it applies the given value first, then issues three library calls that redraw the current setting indicators from stored values, and returns zero.

name: place_item_gadgets
description: Places the gadgets for one preference item, computing each position from the item's record fields and applying the default setting, then returns zero.

name: move_item_and_refresh
description: Clamps a requested item position to the allowed range and, when the position changes, stores it, reprocesses each linked sub-item and redraws the item through library calls before returning zero.

name: draw_selected_entry_and_save
description: Issues a short sequence of drawing and setup calls with fixed mode values and coordinates, draws the entry selected from a table, and records the chosen index for later use.

name: start_timed_delay_request
description: Opens the timer device and sends a timed request whose duration is the first argument in days plus the second in minutes, converted to seconds. Returns one if the request succeeded and zero otherwise.

name: initialise_empty_exec_list
description: Sets up an empty list header in the memory block passed in: the first word points to the tail slot just after it, the tail is cleared, and the last word points back to the header.

name: write_system_configuration_file
description: Replaces the DEVS system-configuration file with a 232-byte block: it deletes any existing copy, creates a new file and writes the block, removing the new file again if the write is short. Returns the block pointer on success and zero otherwise.

name: read_system_configuration_or_defaults
description: Reads the 232-byte DEVS system-configuration block into the buffer passed in. If the file is missing or the read is short, it fills the buffer with default settings instead, and returns the buffer.

name: return_immediately
description: Contains only a return instruction, so it performs no work when called.

name: run_settings_dialog_loop
description: Opens the settings dialog and its message port, draws the items, then waits for messages. A code of 1 restores settings from the backup and a code of 2 saves current settings into it, after which the dialog is closed and zero is returned.

name: await_dialog_save_or_restore
description: Waits for dialog message codes: it saves current settings into the backup when the code is 2, restores them from the backup when the code is 1, then closes the dialog and returns zero.

name: restore_saved_settings
description: Copies the saved backup values back into the current settings, then closes the dialog through two library calls and returns zero.

name: save_current_settings
description: Copies the current settings into the backup values, then closes the dialog through two library calls and returns zero.

name: dispatch_setting_toggle_command
description: Switches on a command code for the settings dialog: codes 69 and 70 return 1 and 2, codes 71 to 77 set or clear a stored option and redraw its indicator, code 78 walks a list of entries, and any other code goes to a default path that returns 1.

name: run_callback_then_succeed
description: Calls one routine with the global variable's address and returns one to signal success.

name: return_without_action
description: Contains only a return instruction, so it performs no work when called.

name: clear_matched_code_word
description: Checks a stored double-word code against a fixed value when a counter equals 15. On a match it runs a routine and clears the stored code.

name: test_value_not_one
description: Returns true when its argument is anything other than one.

name: return_argument_unchanged
description: Returns its single argument unchanged.

name: draw_rectangle_from_table
description: Draws one entry of a coordinate table: it sets a mode, draws a rectangle between two corner positions offset by 20 units from the stored table values, and resets a status byte before returning.

name: find_threshold_table_index
description: Scans a table of 16-bit threshold values until it reaches one that is not below the argument, then returns the index before it, or zero when the first entry already qualifies.

name: decrement_clamped_at_zero
description: Returns the word in the data register minus one, or zero when that word is already zero.

name: decrement_register_value
description: Returns the word in the data register minus one, with no other effect.

name: allocate_and_copy_buffers
description: Allocates six buffers through a library call and copies a table of data into each. If any allocation fails it returns one; otherwise it sets a group of pointers to one common value, bitwise-inverts 258 words of a table, and returns zero.

name: call_setup_then_reset
description: Calls the library setup routine on the global block with an argument of one, then calls another routine with zero.

name: call_library_vector_66
description: Calls one library function at a fixed offset of 66 bytes below the library base held in a global, and returns nothing.

name: call_library_vector_72
description: Calls one library function at a fixed offset of 72 bytes below the library base held in a global, and returns nothing.

name: call_library_vector_222
description: Calls one library function at a fixed offset of 222 bytes below the library base held in a global, and returns nothing.

name: call_library_vector_324
description: Calls one library function at a fixed offset of 324 bytes below the library base held in a global, and returns nothing.

name: draw_item_group_enable_dma
description: Draws three ranges of items chosen by the group argument, issuing a drawing call for each item, then writes the DMA control register with bit 15 set to enable DMA channels. It returns the group argument, or a value from one further routine for group 3.

name: measure_string_length
description: Returns the number of characters before the terminating zero byte in the given string.

name: draw_null_terminated_text
description: Draws a text string on the window's rastport through a graphics library call, passing a length of minus one so the text is taken up to its terminator.

name: draw_selector_frame_outline
description: Draws the outline of a selector frame for the given index, placing a fixed pattern of lines and boxes on the window rastport at positions spaced 34 units apart.

name: draw_settings_panel_fields
description: Draws the settings panel fields selected by a mask. For each set bit it draws that field's box or readout, and the first field shows a numeric value computed from the flag bits.

name: map_nine_to_zero
description: Returns zero when the argument equals nine and eight otherwise.

name: map_one_to_zero
description: Returns zero when the argument equals one and sixteen otherwise.

name: draw_outlined_box
description: Draws a bordered box at a given position and size: it sets a draw mode, then draws the box outline and its edges on the window rastport using the four arguments.

name: draw_status_box_for_flag
description: Draws a fixed-size box on the window rastport at one of two horizontal positions, chosen by whether the argument is zero.

name: draw_default_status_box
description: Draws the box at the default position and size used by the status panel by calling the box drawing routine with four fixed coordinate and size values.

name: format_decimal_number_text
description: Writes a 16-bit number into a text buffer as decimal digits followed by a zero terminator, padding to three digits for values of 100 and above, and returns the end position of the text.

name: divide_long_by_divisor
description: Divides a 32-bit value by a divisor, using a 16-step shift-and-subtract loop for divisors above 16 bits and 16-bit divisions otherwise, and returns the quotient and remainder.

name: multiply_32_bit_integers
description: Multiplies two 32-bit values held in data registers using 16-bit partial products and returns the combined product.

name: stub_self_call_unreached
description: Unreached code that only calls its own entry point and then returns. It is most likely data decoded as instructions, so it has no meaningful behaviour.

name: call_and_return_d1
description: Calls another routine and returns whatever value that routine left in the second data register.

name: negate_result_on_word_flag
description: Calls a routine, then returns its result negated when the secondary word result it leaves in the address register is nonzero.

name: negate_result_on_long_flag
description: Calls a routine, then returns its result negated when the secondary long result it leaves in the address register is nonzero.

name: store_packed_colour_entry
description: Packs red, green and blue values into one 12-bit colour word, stores it in a table at an index counted from 15, and passes the same arguments to the graphics library's colour call.

name: unpack_colour_nibbles_for_display
description: Reads a packed colour word from a table at an index counted from 15, splits it into red, green and blue nibbles, and passes each nibble expanded to 16 bits to a drawing routine with a fixed record and window.

name: create_message_port
description: Allocates a signal bit and a cleared memory block, fills in the port fields with the given name, the current task and the signal bit, then initialises the port's message list or adds the port to the system list. Returns the port, or zero if an allocation fails.

name: delete_message_port
description: Removes the port from the system list when it is named, marks the port as deleted, frees its signal bit and releases its memory block.

name: allocate_typed_record
description: Allocates a cleared 48-byte block, marks it with type code 5 and a zero flag, and stores the argument in it. Returns the block, or zero if the argument is zero or the allocation fails.

name: free_typed_record
description: Marks a 48-byte record as released by setting its status byte to 255 and two fields to minus one, then frees its memory block.

name: run_secondary_dialog_loop
description: Waits on a message port for dialog events, ignoring messages of type 8. A code of 1 restores saved values from a backup and a code of 2 saves current values into it, then the items are redrawn, the window is closed and zero is returned.

name: await_secondary_dialog_code
description: Waits for a message code on the port, ignoring messages of type 8. A code of 1 restores saved values from the backup and a code of 2 saves current values into it, then the dialog is closed and zero is returned.

name: restore_secondary_settings
description: Copies the saved values back into the current settings, runs a further routine when the status byte equals three, and closes the dialog through library calls before returning zero.

name: save_secondary_settings
description: Copies the current settings into the saved backup, runs a further routine when the status byte equals three, and closes the dialog through library calls before returning zero.

name: open_secondary_window_and_draw
description: Opens a window first sized 320 wide and then resized to 640 wide, copies settings tables into place, and draws the window's initial contents through library calls.

name: dispatch_secondary_panel_action
description: Switches on an action code for the secondary panel: code 79 returns 1 and code 83 returns 2, codes 80 to 82 step through entries while drawing them, code 87 cycles a four-state value and redraws it, code 88 processes a pointer selection in a region, and code 89 redraws the whole panel.

name: return_zero
description: Returns zero without doing anything else.

name: draw_colour_nibble_swatches
description: Returns zero when the status byte equals three. Otherwise it reads a packed colour word for the given index, splits it into red, green and blue nibbles, draws three swatches from them and returns the last drawing result.

name: draw_swatches_from_register_index
description: Reads a packed colour word for the index held in a data register, splits it into red, green and blue nibbles and draws three swatches from them, with no status check.

name: store_packed_colour_indexed
description: Packs red, green and blue values into one 12-bit colour word, stores it in a table at the given index plus four, and passes the same arguments to the graphics library's colour call.

name: draw_bevelled_control_frame
description: Draws a frame around one control chosen by index, placing four edges at positions offset by a few units from the control's stored coordinates on the window rastport.

name: call_three_times_minus_one
description: Passes the window, a global block and the value minus one to the same routine three times.

name: draw_option_row_with_state
description: Draws one option row from a column index and a row index. It sets the pen for the row's state, draws the row's box and three text strings at offsets from the coordinates, and calls a further routine when the stored selection matches the row.

name: draw_bitplane_cell_grid
description: Draws a 16 by 16 grid of cells, taking each cell's colour value from the matching bit in two stored 16-bit bitplanes and calling a drawing routine for every cell.

name: set_cell_value_in_bitplanes
description: Writes a two-bit value into the cell at a given column and row by clearing that bit position in two stored 16-bit planes and setting the new bits from the value.

name: draw_selection_highlight
description: Draws a highlight around the currently selected item, locating it from offsets computed from the stored selection index, and draws an extra marker when one check matches.

name: run_settings_window_loop
description: Opens a window, applies its stored values as drawing parameters and waits for messages. Code 1 restores the saved settings from a backup, code 2 saves current settings into it, then the window is closed and zero is returned.

name: await_settings_window_code
description: Waits for a message code on the window port. A code of 2 saves the current settings into the backup and a code of 1 restores them, then the window is closed and zero is returned.

name: restore_settings_window_values
description: Copies the backup values back into the current settings, clears the redraw marker, then closes the window through two library calls and returns zero.

name: save_settings_window_values
description: Copies the current settings into the backup values, clears the redraw marker, then closes the window through two library calls and returns zero.

name: dispatch_settings_window_action
description: Switches on an action code for the settings window: code 44 returns 1 and code 45 applies a sign to three stored values and returns 2. The other cases set or toggle individual option bits and redraw them, and code 64 rebuilds the window with its default values.

name: return_zero_immediately
description: Returns zero without doing anything else.

name: draw_panel_page_with_labels
description: Draws a settings panel page: when its flag argument is nonzero it draws a box and a label, then draws fixed text lines and the 29-character entry selected by the current index from a string table.

name: find_key_index_in_table
description: Searches the first 14 bytes of a table for the given character and returns its index, or 13 when the character is not found.

name: find_key_index_from_one
description: Searches the table from its second entry onward for the given character and returns the index of the first match, or 13 when no entry up to 13 matches.

name: clamp_value_to_bounds
description: Ensures one stored value is at least one, copies it into the active setting when it does not exceed a stored upper limit, then runs a further routine.

name: refresh_stored_value_display
description: Redraws a stored value's display: it draws the current label, caches the value, draws its text with a terminator-based length, and then draws the associated region through a further routine.

name: clamp_paired_values
description: Keeps a pair of stored values consistent by enforcing minimums of one and copying one into the other when a cached limit is exceeded, then runs a further routine.

name: refresh_second_value_display
description: Redraws the second stored value's display: it caches the value, draws its text with a terminator-based length, draws the associated region and then runs a further routine.

name: initialize_preference_entry
description: Checks a cached value and, when it is below one, sets a stored value to one and runs a further routine.

name: refresh_third_value_display
description: Redraws the third stored value's display: it caches the value, draws its text with a terminator-based length, draws the associated region and then runs a further drawing routine.

name: launch_command_with_arguments
description: Program entry for this command: it finds the largest size value in a linked list, builds a buffer of that size with a fixed header word, copies the argument string into a stack buffer and runs the command through a library call. It returns minus one if setup fails and zero otherwise.

name: copy_sixteen_longs_then_call
description: If the destination pointer passed on the stack is non-null, copies sixteen 32-bit values from a fixed offset in a structure held in a register into that destination, then jumps through a function pointer held in another register.

name: launch_command_with_arguments
description: Program entry for this command: it finds the largest size value in a linked list, builds a buffer of that size with a fixed header word, copies the argument string into a stack buffer and runs the command through a library call. It returns minus one if setup fails and zero otherwise.

name: copy_sixteen_longs_then_call
description: If the destination pointer passed on the stack is non-null, copies sixteen 32-bit values from a fixed offset in a structure held in a register into that destination, then jumps through a function pointer held in another register.

name: entry_build_cli_command_string
description: Program entry point that checks whether the process was started from the CLI. The Workbench branch runs setup and library calls, while the CLI branch copies the command name and argument text into a string on the stack and runs the main routine with it.

name: release_message_and_free_buffers
description: Frees two buffers if they were allocated, through a library call, then disables multitasking and replies to a message before returning its argument.

name: call_two_library_vectors
description: Calls two library functions one after the other through a library base register, using two fixed offsets below that base, and returns.

name: attempt_library_call_else_release
description: Returns the result of one library call when it is nonzero; otherwise it runs a library function and the same finishing sequence as the release routine, then returns the value 100.

name: call_alloc_mem
description: Calls the exec library's memory allocation routine through the library base in a register and returns its result.

name: call_free_mem
description: Calls the exec library's memory release routine through the library base in a register and returns its result.

name: call_find_task
description: Calls the exec library's task lookup routine through the library base and returns the task pointer it provides.

name: call_set_signal
description: Calls the exec library's signal control routine through the library base and returns its result.

name: call_add_port
description: Calls the exec library's routine that adds a message port to the system list and returns its result.

name: parse_string_table
description: Splits a command string into tokens separated by spaces, keeping double-quoted text as one token and storing a pointer to each token in a table. With no tokens it opens the file system library and sets up the current task's stream fields; otherwise it fetches the input and output handles and opens the library.

name: allocate_and_init_block
description: Allocates a block sized to the input plus a constant, stores that size inside the block, passes the global block and the block address to another routine, and returns the block address plus a constant offset. It returns zero if the allocation fails.

name: return_result_or_minus_one
description: Calls a routine and returns its result, or minus one when that result is zero.

name: return_minus_one
description: Returns minus one without other work. The code is unreached in the program's flow.

name: free_linked_memory_blocks
description: Walks a singly linked list whose head is held in a global, freeing each node with the size stored at its offset and following the next pointer until the list ends.

name: append_node_to_list
description: Appends a node to a list whose head and tail pointers are held in the first structure: the node's next pointer is cleared, the previous tail is linked to it, and it becomes the tail, and also the head when the list was empty.

name: open_screen_and_run_interface
description: Opens the graphics and intuition libraries and a custom screen, sets its colours and draws the title text, then opens a window with a menu strip. It runs a loop that animates the status frame and reads window messages until its exit flag is set, then closes the screen and libraries.

name: open_numbered_panel_window
description: For a selector from 0 to 7, opens one of eight panel windows at a set position and fills its background with a pen chosen for that panel, then records a status value.

name: open_numbered_panel_stack_arg
description: For a selector from 0 to 7, opens one of eight panel windows at a set position and fills its background with a pen chosen for that panel, then records a status value.

name: draw_buttons_open_panel
description: Redraws the bottom strip of four images and, for selector values 1 and 4, opens the matching small panel window or closes the previous one, then returns the result of a further routine.

name: open_small_status_window
description: Opens a small status window at a fixed position and fills it with pen 6 when the selector is 1, or pen 14 otherwise, then runs a further routine unless a flag is set and returns its result.

name: open_fourteen_pen_status_window
description: Opens a small status window at a fixed position, fills its background with pen 14, then runs a further routine unless a flag is set and returns its result.

name: lock_portal_disk_path
description: Points the task's window pointer at the game window to suppress requesters, builds a path naming the portal volume and a selected digit, and retries a lock on that path until it succeeds. It then restores the window pointer.

name: show_text_panel_window
description: Opens one of several text windows chosen by a selector, fills its background and draws its lines of credits or access messages, then waits for input messages or a delay before closing it.

name: call_dos_open
description: Calls the dos library's Open function through the dos library base held in a global, and returns the result the library leaves in its register.

name: call_dos_close
description: Calls the dos library's Close function through the dos library base held in a global, and returns nothing.

name: call_dos_read
description: Calls the dos library's Read function through the dos library base held in a global, and returns nothing.

name: call_dos_write
description: Calls the dos library's Write function through the dos library base held in a global, and returns nothing.

name: call_dos_input
description: Calls the dos library's Input function through the dos library base held in a global, and returns nothing.

name: call_dos_output
description: Calls the dos library's Output function through the dos library base held in a global, and returns nothing.

name: call_dos_delete_file
description: Calls the dos library's DeleteFile function through the dos library base and returns nothing.

name: call_dos_rename
description: Calls the dos library's Rename function through the dos library base and returns nothing.

name: fill_four_status_bars
description: Fills four rectangles in a horizontal band of the window with pen 4 and returns. If the stack is too small it first extends the stack and runs the command-line parser instead.

name: fill_four_status_bars
description: Fills four rectangles in a horizontal band of the window with pen 4 and returns.

name: fill_pattern_byte_sequence
description: Fills a byte buffer backwards from the given index with a sequence in which each byte is derived from the three bytes before it plus a constant, seeded from the two character arguments.

name: build_and_draw_image_grid
description: Allocates a 1505-byte buffer, fills it with pixel words computed by a routine, then draws a grid of four rows by five images from it onto the window and frees the buffer.

name: build_and_draw_image_grid
description: Allocates a 1505-byte buffer, fills it with pixel words computed by a routine, then draws a grid of four rows by five images from it onto the window and frees the buffer.

name: fill_table_draw_grid
description: Continues the image grid build: it clears a run of table entries, sets two marker words, fills the remaining entries from a routine's results, draws the four by five image grid and frees the buffer.

name: draw_image_grid_tail
description: Sets two marker words, fills the remaining table entries from a routine's results, draws the four by five image grid and frees the buffer.

name: fill_rest_and_draw_grid
description: Sets two table words, fills the remaining entries with routine values, then draws the four by five image grid and frees the buffer.

name: fill_flag_table_draw_grid
description: Fills table entries from routine results with one of two fixed words, clears the remaining entries, draws the four by five image grid and frees the buffer.

name: fill_table_words_draw_grid
description: Fills table entries with fixed words chosen by a routine's results, clears the remaining entries, draws the four by five image grid and frees the buffer.

name: clear_tail_and_draw_grid
description: Clears the last table entries, draws the four by five image grid and frees the buffer.

name: clear_tail_entries_and_free
description: Clears the final table entries, draws the four by five image grid and frees the buffer.

name: draw_image_grid_and_free
description: Draws the four by five image grid from the buffer onto the window, then frees the buffer.

name: draw_remaining_grid_rows
description: Advances the row offset and draws the rest of the four by five image grid row by row, then frees the buffer.

name: free_image_buffer
description: Frees the 1505-byte image buffer held in the frame.

name: render_full_image_buffer
description: Allocates a 32000-byte image buffer, fills it with image words for each row using a routine to compute values, draws the result with one image draw call, and frees the buffer.

name: draw_horizontal_rule_lines
description: Draws two sets of six horizontal lines across the window, first with pen 1 and then with pen 2, spaced 15 units apart. If the stack is too small it first extends it and runs the command-line parser instead.

name: draw_horizontal_rule_lines
description: Draws two sets of six horizontal lines across the window, first with pen 1 and then with pen 2, spaced 15 units apart.

name: draw_second_rule_line_set
description: Draws two sets of six horizontal lines across the window in pen 2, spaced 15 units apart, starting from a fixed line.

name: render_palette_image_buffer
description: Allocates a 32000-byte buffer, fills it row by row with image words chosen by a routine's values and a four-way pen selection, draws the result with one image call and frees the buffer. If the stack is too small it first extends it.

name: render_full_image_buffer
description: Allocates a 32000-byte image buffer, fills it with image words for each row using a routine to compute values, draws the result with one image draw call, and frees the buffer.

name: render_image_rows_continue
description: Continues the row-by-row image fill of the 32000-byte buffer, choosing source words from a routine's results for each row, and after the last row draws the buffer with one image call and frees it.
